label: LitRPG / progression
description: Game-system or progression fantasy: numbers, builds, dungeons and clever problem-solving, with steady visible growth.
voice: First or close third person, past tense; the protagonist thinks like a gamer or an engineer: tests, theories, optimisation.
System messages and stat blocks are consistent in format and appear only when something changes.
Growth is steady and earned; every gain is used soon after.
Problems are solved with clever build choices and teamwork, not just bigger numbers.
Humour from the system's quirks and the hero's theorycrafting.
End chapters on a new unlock, a threat that outlevels them, or a question about the system.

structure.guide: Entry into the system or the dungeon, with an immediate lethal problem.
structure.then: Learn the rules through experiments; each chapter one new mechanic.

structure.guide: The class or build choice that defines the book, with a trade-off.
The first dungeon boss that requires a clever plan.
structure.then: Level, loot, allies; a rival party.

structure.guide: The system reveals a hidden layer, a quest chain or a flaw that changes the goal.
Death penalty, lost gear or a betrayed party.
The big fight where the unusual build pays off.
A new tier, zone or rank that resets the scale.

outline_guidance: Every chapter has a problem the protagonist solves with a specific mechanic or build choice; name the mechanic in the line.
outline_example: Aggro Math | In the flooded third floor of the Glass Warren, Theo Park kites the eel queen by stacking his useless Splash skill on the party's tank | He discovers that status effects stack without a cap | The queen's second phase eats the tank's shield
scene_guidance: Show the plan, then show it going wrong.
worldbuilding: The system's rules and its exploits
The zones and their level ranges
Who else is in the system and why
naming: Whatever fits the setting; skills and items get short, punchy names.
sample:
[Splash (Lv 1): 2 water damage. Applies Wet.]

It was the worst skill in the game. Theo had checked the forums.

He cast it anyway, once, twice, four times, onto the tank's back while Rhee shouted things about his mother.

[Wet x4]

The eel queen's lightning hit Rhee, rolled off the water on his armour, and went looking for the nearest wet thing that was not Rhee.

It found the eel queen.
